title: Circles, squares and triangles
keyIdea: A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. A square has 4 straight sides that are all the same length and 4 corners. A rectangle has 4 sides too, 2 long and 2 short. A circle is round all the way, with no straight sides and no corners. Turning a shape round or making it bigger does not change its name, but a gap or a bendy side does. Shapes are all around: a plate is a circle, a window can be a square, a door is a rectangle and half a sandwich can be a triangle.

kid: Run your finger round a shape. A straight side is like a ruler. A corner is a pointy bit where two sides meet.
A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. Tip it over, or make it tall and thin. It is still a triangle. But the sides must all join up and be straight.
A square has 4 sides, all the same. Stand it on a corner and it is still a square. A rectangle has 4 sides too: 2 long and 2 short. A door is a rectangle.
A circle is round all the way, like a plate or a clock. It has no corners. An egg is round too, but it is long. That shape is an oval.
adult: This is early shape and space. Development Matters asks three and four year olds to talk about 2D shapes such as circles, rectangles and triangles. They use words like sides, corners, straight, flat and round. In Reception they turn and move shapes. In Year 1 they name common 2D shapes in different sizes and turned different ways.

What matters is the rule, not the picture. A triangle is any closed shape with 3 straight sides. A square has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners (right angles). A rectangle has 4 square corners, and its opposite sides are equal. Strictly, a square is a special rectangle, but at this age children tell them apart by side length. A circle has one curved edge and no corners (vertices).

Common mistakes: calling a square on its point a diamond, as if it were a new shape; thinking only an upright triangle with equal sides counts; calling every 4-sided shape a square; calling an oval a circle; and accepting a shape with a gap or a curved side as a triangle. These slips come from only seeing textbook pictures. Show shapes turned, stretched and in real things.

In the lab your child taps each corner of a triangle, a square and a rectangle to count it, and finds that a circle has none. Then they sort triangles from look-alikes, and squares from rectangles, using marks that show equal sides. They build each shape from short and long sticks, and hunt for the four shapes in a room.

familyTip: Go on a shape walk at home or outside. Point and ask: is that a circle, a square, a triangle or a rectangle? How many corners can you count? Cut a sandwich into triangles, then into squares.

visual.caption: How many straight sides? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap corners to count them, sort real triangles and squares from look-alikes, make shapes from sticks, and hunt for shapes in a room.

practice.prompt: How many corners does a square have?
practice.hint: Touch each pointy corner and count.
practice.explain: A square has 4 corners and 4 straight sides, all the same.

practice.prompt: You have {n} triangles. How many corners is that in all? Each triangle has 3.
practice.hint: Count 3 for each triangle: 3, 6, 9 and so on.
practice.explain: {n} triangles with 3 corners each make {=3*n} corners.

practice.hint: A circle is round the same all the way.
practice.explain: A coin is a circle. An egg is round but long, so it is an oval. A book has corners.

practice.prompt: You have {n} squares. How many sides is that in all? Each square has 4.
practice.hint: Count 4 for each square: 4, 8 and so on.
practice.explain: {n} squares with 4 sides each make {=4*n} sides.

pool.prompt: A triangle is turned upside down. What is it now?
pool.hint: Count its sides and corners again.
pool.explain: It still has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. Turning it round does not change it.

pool.prompt: A shape has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. What is it?
pool.explain: The sides are not all the same, so it is not a square. 2 long and 2 short is a rectangle.

pool.prompt: How many corners does a circle have?
pool.hint: Run your finger round it. Is there a pointy bit?
pool.explain: A circle is round all the way, so it has no corners and no straight sides.

pool.prompt: A square stands on one corner. What is it?
pool.hint: Are its 4 sides still all the same?
pool.explain: Its 4 sides are all still the same, so it is a square, just turned.

pool.prompt: A shape has 3 straight sides, but there is a gap at the top. Is it a triangle?
choices: No, the sides must join up
pool.hint: Do the sides go all the way round?
pool.explain: A triangle is closed. Its 3 sides must join up with no gap.

choices: Half a sandwich cut corner to corner
pool.hint: Look for 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short.
pool.explain: A door has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. A plate is a circle, and the sandwich half is a triangle.

pool.prompt: You make {n} triangles out of sticks. Each one needs 3 sticks. How many sticks do you need?
pool.explain: {n} triangles need 3 sticks each, so {=3*n} sticks.

choices: A slice of pizza with straight sides
pool.hint: Look for 3 straight sides and 3 corners.
pool.explain: Cut with straight sides, a pizza slice has 3 sides and 3 corners. A wheel is a circle and a window has 4 sides.

pool.prompt: You draw {n} rectangles. Each one has 4 corners. How many corners is that?
pool.hint: Count 4 corners for each rectangle: 4, 8, 12 and so on.
pool.explain: {n} rectangles with 4 corners each make {=4*n} corners.
